Tap dice to build a pool; the number on the left is how many each tap adds. Hold a die for advantage, exploding, and the rest. Any number of sides works, from d1 to d1000, so a d17 or a d57 is just as valid. Rolls stay on your device.

v5:5
five dice, no Hunger
v5:8h3
eight dice, three of them Hunger
v5:8h3@3
the same against difficulty 3
4d6
ordinary dice still roll as ordinary dice

Hunger dice replace dice in the pool rather than adding to it, so the pool size is whatever you set. Every die showing 6 or more is a success, and each pair of 10s adds two more on top. Set a difficulty and the roll resolves itself — a win with a pair of 10s is a Critical, and a Messy Critical if one of those 10s is on a Hunger die; a loss with a Hunger 1 is a Bestial Failure. Leave the difficulty unset and the roll reports its successes and lets the table call it.

The dice show symbols the way the official ones do — a fang for a success, the bite for a 10, a skull for a Hunger 1, and nothing at all below 6. The numbers they landed on are in the line under the result and in the history.

4dF
four Fudge dice — the standard roll
4dF+2
with a +2 skill
6dF-1
any number of dice, and a penalty

Each Fudge die is +, −, or blank — two of each on a d6 — so it reads +1, −1, or 0. The result is the net total (−4 to +4 for four dice) plus your modifier, and it lands on the Fate ladder: Mediocre, Average, Fair, Good, Great, and up.

gen:2A+2D
two Ability, two Difficulty
gen:1P+1A+3D
a Proficiency, an Ability, three Difficulty
gen:2A+1B+2D+1C
Boost and Challenge in the mix

Six narrative dice: Ability (green), Proficiency (yellow), Boost (blue) roll toward success; Difficulty (purple), Challenge (red), Setback (grey) roll against you. Tap a chip to add that die, hold it to remove one.

Success (▲) cancels Failure (▼) and Advantage (◆) cancels Threat (✕), so the result is what is left on each axis. A Triumph (★, on the Proficiency die) is a success that also triggers something great; a Despair (its inverted twin, on the Challenge die) is a failure that goes badly wrong. Both survive cancellation.

sw:2A+2D
two Ability, two Difficulty
sw:1P+1A+2D
a trained check
sw:3F
three Force dice (a Force power)

The same narrative dice as Genesys — success/failure and advantage/threat cancel, with Triumph and Despair on the yellow and red dice — plus the white Force die. Its Light (pale) and Dark (violet) pips are a separate result that powers Force abilities; they don't touch the success/advantage tally. Roll a handful of Force dice on their own for a Force check.

dh:
the Duality Dice — Hope d12 + Fear d12
dh:+2
with a modifier (negatives too: dh:-1)
dh:@15
against difficulty 15
dh:adv2@15
with two advantage dice, vs 15

Roll two d12 — a gold Hope die and a violet Fear die — and add them. The higher die sets the tone: with Hope hands you a Hope, with Fear hands the GM a Fear. Matching dice are a Critical Success — it succeeds no matter the total, and comes with Hope. Set a difficulty and the roll resolves to success or failure.

Each advantage adds a d6 and each disadvantage subtracts one; they cancel one-for-one, and stack past one (an ally's Help adds another). Tap the buttons to add them, hold to remove. The Roll Duality button throws the Hope + Fear; the dice below it roll anything else — weapon damage and the rest.

ct:8
eight d10 — count the hits
ct:8@4
the same, against difficulty 4
ct:5@6
a five-die pool at a hard task

CthulhuTech 2e is a pool of coin-flips. Roll d10 equal to your Attribute + Skill; every even die is a Hit (it glows green), every odd one misses. Count your hits and meet the Difficulty — roughly 3 for a simple task up to 6 or 7 for the near-impossible. Leave the difficulty unset and it just reports the hits.

tor:3@14
a Feat die + 3 Success dice, vs 14
tor:2fav@16
favoured — roll two Feat dice, keep the best
tor:3w@18
Weary — Success dice of 1-3 count as 0

Always roll one Feat die (a d12: 1-10, plus the Gandalf rune = automatic success and the Eye of Sauron = 0) with a pool of Success dice (d6). Total them and meet the Target Number. Each 6 is a Tengwar rune: one is a Great success, two or more Extraordinary. Favoured / ill-favoured rolls two Feat dice and keeps the best / worst; Weary makes Success dice of 1-3 count for nothing.

pbta:
roll 2d6
pbta:+2
2d6 plus your stat
pbta:-1
2d6 with a penalty

Powered by the Apocalypse: roll 2d6 and add the relevant stat. 10+ is a Strong Hit, 7-9 a Weak Hit (you get it, but with a cost), 6 or under a Miss. Set the modifier below, or type it.

mist:
roll 2d6
mist:+1
2d6 plus your Power
mist:-2
2d6 with Weakness against you

The Mist Engine (City of Mist, Legend in the Mist) rolls 2d6 plus your net Power. 10+ is a Success, 7-9 a Consequence (you succeed with a complication), 6 or under a Failure. Set the modifier below, or type it.

ms:c@35
Check/Save — roll d100 under 35
ms:c@35e
the same, Expert skill (+15 → under 50)
ms:c@35adv
Advantage — roll twice, keep the better
ms:p@8
Panic — roll d20 over Stress 8

Mothership rolls 1d100 under your Stat or Save: less than the number succeeds, a fail costs 1 Stress. 00 always crits, 99 always crit-fails, 90-99 always fails, and doubles are a Critical. A Skill tier (Trained +10, Expert +15, Master +20) raises the number you roll under. Panic rolls a d20 over your Stress; roll at or under it and you Panic — look up the die on your own Panic Table. Stress is tracked here: it climbs on failed rolls and is what Panic rolls against. Damage and Wounds are ordinary dice — type 4d10 or tap the strip.

This is the single-file build: it already works offline, and can be copied anywhere.

Source on GitHub

An unofficial fan tool — not affiliated with or endorsed by the makers of the games it can roll for.

Dice system

The system recolours the app and changes the dice you tap. Typed notation still means what it says — 4d6 is four six-sided dice in any mode.
